The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=h(x)$ are given above. Find ${p}^{′}(-1)$ where $p(x)=f(x)h(x).$

${p}^{′}(-1)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The product rule for derivatives gives

$$
{p}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot h(x)+f(x)\cdot {h}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{p}^{′}(-1)={f}^{′}(-1)\cdot h(-1)+f(-1)\cdot {h}^{′}(-1).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(-1)=1$ and $h(-1)=2.$

Additionally,

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-2,1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-1)=-1.$

- The slope of $h(x)$ on $x\in (-2,1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${h}^{′}(-1)=-1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(-1) & ={f}^{′}(-1)\cdot h(-1)+f(-1)\cdot {h}^{′}(-1) \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2+1\cdot (-1) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
